claim: The cold trap must hold 14 K for Ne adsorption and then be heated to 100 K to release Ne, so the trap temperature must span 14-100 K.

document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050

verification.note: Verified in Beyerle et al. 2000 (Eawag PDF p.2044): the CCT is held at 14 K for Ne adsorption, and 'the CCT is heated to 100 K to release Ne'. The quote is an elided composite of real sentences. A 14-100 K range is correct.

claim: Quantitative Ne adsorption needs the trap at 14 K or colder.

document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050

verification.note: Verbatim on p.2044: 'cryogenic cold trap (CCT) at 14 K containing a high porosity filter of sintered stainless steel (Nupro SS-2FE-5, 0.5 um) that adsorbs Ne quantitatively'. at_most 14 K is justified.

document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050
